What has Mat built with AI?.answer:
Mostly AI that runs on real systems:
• Kapti: a meeting assistant that transcribes and writes notes entirely on-device (Whisper/Parakeet and llama.cpp), with a local knowledge base that surfaces your own notes during calls.
• AGP: an AI phone receptionist and about 140 n8n workflows for local businesses, live with 5 clients.
• Forge: a training app with a self-hosted AI coach that logs food from a photo or a sentence.
• Agentic Builder: a Claude Code plugin with 19 role agents and least-privilege guardrails.
• This site: the agent you're talking to, plus a job-tailoring feature.

How is the homelab run as code?.answer: 36 Docker Compose stacks live in one Git repo, and deploys go through a gate: deploy.sh refuses to run unless validate.sh passes. It requires every image pinned by digest, a declared contract per stack (tier, wave, data class, purpose, backup paths), a managed label, and a clean secrets scan. The rebuild ran side by side with the old setup while services moved over one at a time.

Is he a fit for a DevOps role?.answer: For a platform or DevOps role, the strongest evidence is six years as a systems administrator (servers, networking, backups, identity) plus the homelab: 36 services as code with digest-pinned images, policy-gated deploys, Prometheus alerting and SSO. He also runs AGP's production stack (Docker, Traefik, Postgres, queue-mode n8n). Kubernetes isn't in his profile. For a specific posting, the "Tailor to a job" page gives a full fit report.

What's Kapti?.answer: Kapti is a Windows meeting assistant that never phones home. It records the mic and system audio as separate tracks, transcribes on-device, and has a local LLM write the summary, decisions and action items. Any cloud feature is opt-in, and every request goes through one allow-listed gateway that CI enforces. It's built in Rust with Tauri 2, 242 IPC commands and 1,144 Rust tests.
